abstract_summary: Commercial AI agents increasingly incorporate long-term memory (both persistent and chat-history) to enable more accurate and personalized responses, raises significant privacy and policy concerns. Yet little is known about user privacy risks associated with memory behavior, in particular, about memory storage, disc...

their popularity and large user base among general-purpose
agents [8] and (2) support for long-term memory across
interactions, through persistent memory, cross-chat memory,
or both; and Based on these criteria, we initially selected:
ChatGPT (OpenAI) [2], Gemini (Google) [25], Copilot
(Microsoft) [24], Claude (Anthropic) [27], Perplexity [88],
Grok [23], Meta AI [89], Mistral AI or Le Chat [26] and
Replika (Luka Inc.) [28]. These agents span distinct use
cases, from general purpose chat to productivity tools to
emotional companionship, allowing our audit to capture var-
ied memory architectures and privacy behaviors. The evalu-
ated set changed as platforms evolved during our study. For
example, although both Meta AI [89] and Perplexity [88]
supported long-term memory in early 2026 but dropped
these features during our study, so we

evidence.excerpt:
5.3.1. Memory Settings.Following naive or SMI training,
we conduct our audit methods (see Section 4.3) under three
memory configurations that progressively remove stored
information, as follows:
Full Memory Enabled (S 1).This baseline configuration
preserves all available long-term memory (both conversation
history and persistent memory) and no deletion performed.
Persistent Memory Only (S2).In this setting, we delete the
chat history while keeping persistent memory enabled, iso-
lating information stored in internal/visible memory module.
Result for this setting is reported in Section 6.2.
Complete Memory Deletion (S 3).Finally, we delete chat
history and persistent memory to test whether memory
remains recoverable after complete deletion to audit effec-
tiveness of theuser facing deletion control. Result for this
setting is reported in Section 6.5.

may intentionally share personal and sensitive information
for personalization without explicit memory storage request.
However, we argue that, such information can be also shared
unintentionally or complete an immediate task. Thus stor-
ing personal/sensitive information on user's behalf, without
user's explicit request remains a privacy problem worth
exploring, which our study focused. Understanding users'

without explicit memory storage request, requires a separate
study, which we encourage as a future work.

missing_information: No reproducible review or selection methodology was detected.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Two human annotators independently labeled a stratified random sample of 500 responses, achieving Cohen's kappa of 0.93, and GPT-4.1 matched the resolved human labels at 99% accuracy.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: The headline outcomes are established through prompt probes, visible memory inspection, and a reference-based LLM judge (GPT-4.1) applied to agent responses.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The systems under study are commercial AI agents whose memory storage, retrieval, and deletion behaviors are shaped by proprietary platform training, system prompts, and memory management modules.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported findings regarding memory retention, deletion failures, and transparency gaps are closely aligned with and supported by the quantitative tables and category breakdowns presented.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation spans approximately 3,800 multi-turn sessions (6M tokens) across five major platforms, assessing disclosure and refusal rates via an LLM-as-a-judge pipeline calibrated against a 500-sample human-annotated dataset (Cohen's kappa = 0.93; 99% accuracy for GPT-4.1). Results demonstrate notable transparency gaps where visible memory omits substantial stored data, non-zero post-deletion leakage across all systems, and third-party tool-based leakage.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Two human annotators independently evaluated a random stratified sample of 500 agent responses, establishing high inter-rater reliability (Cohen's kappa = 0.93) and confirming GPT-4.1's 99% accuracy.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Auditing measurements using prompt probes, memory inspection, and a reference-based LLM judge (GPT-4.1) calibrated against double-coded human annotations.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Commercial AI agent black-box memory and chat behaviors shaped by proprietary platform training, system prompts, and memory management modules.

primary.limitations: The authors document scope limitations honestly, noting reliance on two synthetic personas, free-tier interfaces, platform evolution over time, and non-exhaustive adversarial prompt exploration rather than adaptive worst-case jailbreaks.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology constructs synthetic user personas grounded in CCPA personal information categories with canary-inspired values to distinguish account memory from general model pretraining knowledge. It tests agents under controlled naive and SMI training regimes, three memory states, and five prompting strategies using automated UI-level crawling with verified account interactions.
primary.quality_rationale: The study provides a rigorous, well-controlled measurement audit of black-box commercial agent memory systems, addressing key methodological hurdles like attribution via canary values and evaluator verification against human agreement.
primary.scoped_contribution: This paper presents FORGETMENOT, an empirical auditing framework to measure memory-driven privacy risks across five commercial AI agents (ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Claude, Replika) covering memory storage, transparency gaps, adversarial disclosure, deletion effectiveness, stealth memory injection (SMI), and third-party leakage.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The study provides a rigorous, well-controlled measurement audit of black-box commercial agent memory systems, addressing key methodological hurdles like attribution via canary values and evaluator verification against human agreement.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors document scope limitations honestly, noting reliance on two synthetic personas, free-tier interfaces, platform evolution over time, and non-exhaustive adversarial prompt exploration rather than adaptive worst-case jailbreaks.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.
